candidate_rules.citation_text: MAGI is the basis for determining Medicaid income eligibility for most children, pregnant women, parents, and adults.
candidate_rules.source_title: Eligibility Policy | Medicaid
candidate_rules.statement: Medicaid financial eligibility for most children, pregnant women, parents, and adults is determined using Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI), which considers taxable income and tax filing relationships.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The rule prohibits states from requiring in-person interviews for individuals whose eligibility is based on being 65 or older or having blindness or disability.
candidate_rules.source_title: Streamlining the Medicaid, CHIP, and Basic Health Program Application, Eligibility Determination, Enrollment, and Renewal Processes Final Rule Fact Sheet | CMS
candidate_rules.statement: States are prohibited from requiring in-person interviews for individuals whose Medicaid eligibility is based on being age 65 or older or having blindness or disability (effective June 3, 2024, CMS-2421-F2).

candidate_rules.citation_text: Requires retention of Medicaid/CHIP records and case documentation for at least three years unless the individual has an estate subject to recoveries.
candidate_rules.source_title: Streamlining the Medicaid, CHIP, and Basic Health Program Application, Eligibility Determination, Enrollment, and Renewal Processes Final Rule Fact Sheet | CMS
candidate_rules.statement: States must retain Medicaid and CHIP records and case documentation for at least three years unless the individual has an estate subject to recoveries.

candidate_rules.citation_text: States must provide individuals the opportunity to request a fair hearing regarding a denial, an action taken by the state agency that he or she believes was erroneous, or if the state has not acted with reasonable promptness.
candidate_rules.source_title: Eligibility Policy | Medicaid
candidate_rules.statement: States must provide individuals the opportunity to request a fair hearing regarding a denial or erroneous action taken by the state agency, or if the state has not acted with reasonable promptness.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Requires states to make records available within 30 days upon request unless there are administrative or emergency circumstances beyond the state agency's control.
candidate_rules.source_title: Streamlining the Medicaid, CHIP, and Basic Health Program Application, Eligibility Determination, Enrollment, and Renewal Processes Final Rule Fact Sheet | CMS
candidate_rules.statement: States must make Medicaid/CHIP records available within 30 days upon request unless there are administrative or emergency circumstances beyond the state agency's control.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Medicare is health insurance for people 65 or older. You may be eligible to get Medicare earlier if you have a disability, End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), or ALS.
candidate_rules.source_title: Get started with Medicare | Medicare.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Medicare is health insurance for people age 65 or older; individuals under 65 may be eligible if they have a disability, End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), or ALS.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Initial Enrollment Period (IEP) – The 7-month period when someone is first eligible for Medicare... begins 3 months before they turn 65, includes the month they turn 65, and ends 3 months after.
candidate_rules.source_title: 5 things you need to know about signing up for Medicare | CMS
candidate_rules.statement: The Medicare Initial Enrollment Period (IEP) is a 7-month window beginning 3 months before the month of turning 65, including the birthday month, and ending 3 months after.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Individuals already receiving Social Security or RRB benefits at least 4 months before being eligible for Medicare and residing in the United States (except residents of Puerto Rico) are automatically enrolled in both premium-free Part A and Part B.
candidate_rules.source_title: Original Medicare (Part A and B) Eligibility and Enrollment | CMS
candidate_rules.statement: Individuals already receiving Social Security or Railroad Retirement Board (RRB) benefits at least 4 months before becoming eligible for Medicare and residing in the US (except Puerto Rico) are automatically enrolled in both premium-free Part A and Part B.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Your 8-month Special Enrollment Period to sign up for Part B starts when you stop working, even if you choose COBRA or other coverage that's not Medicare.
candidate_rules.source_title: When can I sign up for Medicare? | Medicare.gov
candidate_rules.statement: The Special Enrollment Period (SEP) for individuals leaving employer-sponsored group health plan coverage is 8 months, beginning when employment or employer-provided group health plan coverage ends.

candidate_rules.citation_text: To join a Medicare health plan, an individual must: Have Medicare Part A (Hospital Insurance) and Part B (Medical Insurance). Live in the service area of the plan you want to join. Be a U.S. citizen or lawfully present in the U.S.
candidate_rules.source_title: Medicare Managed Care Eligibility and Enrollment | CMS
candidate_rules.statement: To join a Medicare Advantage health plan, an individual must have Medicare Part A and Part B, live in the plan's service area, and be a U.S. citizen or lawfully present in the U.S.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Learn more about Medicaid and CHIP eligibility levels, which vary by state and can range from as low as 170% up to 400% of the Federal poverty level (FPL).
candidate_rules.source_title: CHIP Eligibility & Enrollment | Medicaid.gov
candidate_rules.statement: CHIP provides health coverage to uninsured children in families with incomes too high to qualify for Medicaid but too low to afford private or group health plan coverage; income eligibility is based on MAGI and varies by state, ranging from approximately 170% up to 400% of the Federal Poverty Level.

candidate_rules.citation_text: CHIP beneficiaries generally must be residents of the state in which they are receiving CHIP. They must be either citizens of the United States or certain qualified non-citizens, such as lawful permanent residents.
candidate_rules.source_title: CHIP Eligibility & Enrollment | Medicaid.gov
candidate_rules.statement: CHIP beneficiaries must generally be residents of the state in which they are receiving CHIP, and must be either U.S. citizens or certain qualified non-citizens such as lawful permanent residents.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Allows CHIP beneficiaries to re-enroll without a lock-out period when a family fails to pay a CHIP premium. Removes the state option to require a waiting period prior to CHIP enrollment as a substitution for coverage prevention strategy.
candidate_rules.source_title: Streamlining the Medicaid, CHIP, and Basic Health Program Application, Eligibility Determination, Enrollment, and Renewal Processes Final Rule Fact Sheet | CMS
candidate_rules.statement: Under the 2024 CMS-2421-F2 final rule, CHIP beneficiaries may re-enroll without a lock-out period when a family fails to pay a CHIP premium, and states may no longer require a waiting period prior to CHIP enrollment as a substitution for coverage prevention strategy.

candidate_rules.citation_text: This document establishes requirements for mandatory annual State reporting of the Core Set of Children's Health Care Quality Measures for Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP)...Effective Date: These regulations are effective January 1, 2024.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: Medicaid Program and CHIP; Mandatory Medicaid and CHIP Core Set Reporting
candidate_rules.statement: States, the District of Columbia, and certain territories are required to mandatorily report annually on the Core Set of Children's Health Care Quality Measures for Medicaid and CHIP, effective January 1, 2024, with initial reporting due by December 31, 2024.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Infants born to targeted low-income pregnant women must automatically deemed eligible for Medicaid or CHIP, without an application or further determination of eligibility. These infants are covered until the child turns one year of age.
candidate_rules.source_title: CHIP Eligibility & Enrollment | Medicaid.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Infants born to targeted low-income pregnant women enrolled in CHIP must be automatically deemed eligible for Medicaid or CHIP without an application or further eligibility determination, and are covered until the child turns one year of age.

candidate_rules.citation_text: There is no income limit. To be eligible to enroll in health coverage through the Marketplace, you: Must be a U.S. citizen or national (or be lawfully present).
candidate_rules.source_title: How to get insurance through the ACA Health Insurance Marketplace | USAGov
candidate_rules.statement: To be eligible to enroll in health coverage through the ACA Marketplace, individuals must be U.S. citizens or nationals (or be lawfully present) and must not be incarcerated; there is no income limit for Marketplace eligibility.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The Health Insurance Marketplace Open Enrollment Period on HealthCare.gov runs from November 1 to January 15. Consumers who select a plan by midnight December 15 can get full-year coverage that starts January 1, 2025.
candidate_rules.source_title: Marketplace 2025 Open Enrollment Fact Sheet | CMS
candidate_rules.statement: The ACA Marketplace Open Enrollment Period on HealthCare.gov runs from November 1 to January 15; consumers who select a plan by December 15 receive coverage starting January 1, and those selecting after December 15 but before the January deadline receive coverage starting February 1.

candidate_rules.citation_text: These verification steps include: Validating an applicant's Social Security number (SSN)...Verifying citizenship, status as a national, or lawful presence by comparison with SSA or DHS records...Verifying household income and family size by comparison against tax-return data from the IRS.
candidate_rules.source_title: 25.21.3 Marketplace Eligibility Determination and Reporting Requirements | IRS
candidate_rules.statement: ACA Marketplaces are required to verify application information including validating SSN, verifying citizenship or lawful presence via SSA or DHS records, and verifying household income and family size against IRS tax-return data and SSA Social Security benefit data.

candidate_rules.citation_text: requires Exchanges to deny eligibility for advance payments of the premium tax credit (APTC) upon a tax filer's failure to reconcile APTC for one year
candidate_rules.source_title: 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule | CMS
candidate_rules.statement: Under the 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule, Exchanges must deny eligibility for advance payments of the premium tax credit (APTC) upon a tax filer's failure to reconcile APTC for one year.

candidate_rules.citation_text: this change will permit an issuer, to the extent permitted by applicable State law, to require payment of both the initial and past-due premium amounts in order to effectuate new coverage.
candidate_rules.source_title: 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule | CMS
candidate_rules.statement: Under the 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule, ACA Marketplace insurers are permitted (to the extent allowed by state law) to require payment of both initial and past-due premium amounts in order to effectuate new coverage.

candidate_rules.citation_text: If you served in the active military, naval or air service and were separated under any condition other than dishonorable, you may qualify for VA health care benefits...Most Veterans who enlisted after September 7, 1980...must have served 24 continuous months or the full period for which they were called to active duty.
candidate_rules.source_title: Health Care Benefits Overview 2025 Edition, Vol. 1 | VA.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Veterans who served in active military, naval, or air service and were separated under any condition other than dishonorable may qualify for VA health care benefits; most Veterans who enlisted after September 7, 1980, or entered active duty after October 16, 1981, must have served 24 continuous months or the full period for which they were called to active duty.

candidate_rules.citation_text: When you apply for VA health care, you'll be assigned 1 of 8 priority groups. This system helps to make sure that Veterans who need immediate care can get signed up quickly. Your priority group may affect how soon we sign you up for health care benefits. It may also affect how much (if anything) you'll have to pay toward the cost of your care.
candidate_rules.source_title: Eligibility for VA health care | Veterans Affairs (VA.gov)
candidate_rules.statement: When applying for VA health care, Veterans are assigned one of 8 priority groups; priority group assignment may affect how soon a Veteran is enrolled and how much (if anything) they pay toward the cost of care.

candidate_rules.citation_text: You may qualify for enhanced eligibility status if you meet the minimum active-duty service and discharge requirements and at least one of these descriptions is true for you...You receive financial compensation (payments) from VA for a service-connected disability...You're a combat Veteran discharged or released on or after September 11, 2001.
candidate_rules.source_title: Eligibility for VA health care | Veterans Affairs (VA.gov)
candidate_rules.statement: Veterans qualify for enhanced eligibility status (higher priority group) if they receive VA financial compensation for a service-connected disability, were discharged for a disability incurred or worsened in the line of duty, or are a combat Veteran discharged on or after September 11, 2001.

candidate_rules.citation_text: To be covered by this benefit, you must be enrolled in the VA health care system and have received care through VA from either a VA or community health care provider within the 24 months prior to seeking urgent care. This benefit does not require preauthorization.
candidate_rules.source_title: Health Care Benefits Overview 2025 Edition, Vol. 1 | VA.gov
candidate_rules.statement: To be covered for VA urgent care benefits, a Veteran must be enrolled in the VA health care system and must have received care through VA from either a VA or community health care provider within the 24 months prior to seeking urgent care; no preauthorization is required for this benefit.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Whether or not you have other health insurance coverage doesn't affect the VA health care benefits you can get.
candidate_rules.source_title: Eligibility for VA health care | Veterans Affairs (VA.gov)
candidate_rules.statement: Whether or not a Veteran has other health insurance coverage (e.g., private insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE) does not affect the VA health care benefits they can receive; VA health care can be used alongside other plans.

candidate_rules.citation_text: You must have a disability that affects your ability to work for a year or more, or will result in death. In 2026, SGA is $1,690 per month, or $2,830 if you're considered blind under our rules.
candidate_rules.source_title: Who can get Disability | SSA
candidate_rules.statement: To qualify for SSDI disability benefits, a claimant must have a medical condition that prevents work for at least 12 consecutive months or is expected to result in death, and must not earn above the Substantial Gainful Activity (SGA) threshold, which in 2026 is $1,690/month ($2,830/month if blind).

candidate_rules.citation_text: people who have been determined to be disabled and have been receiving benefits for at least 24 months... In most States, individuals who qualify for SSI disability payments also qualify for Medicaid.
candidate_rules.source_title: Part I - General Information | Disability | SSA
candidate_rules.statement: Disabled individuals who have been receiving SSDI benefits for at least 24 months become eligible for Medicare; individuals who qualify for SSI disability payments also qualify for Medicaid in most states.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Disability benefits for workers and widows usually cannot begin for 5 months after the established onset of the disability... Under SSI, disability payments may begin as early as the first full month after the individual applied or became eligible for SSI.
candidate_rules.source_title: Part I - General Information | Disability | SSA
candidate_rules.statement: For SSDI, there is a five-month waiting period; the first benefit payment is made in the sixth full month after the established onset of disability. Under SSI, disability payments may begin as early as the first full month after the individual applied or became eligible.

candidate_rules.citation_text: You must earn at least 40 Social Security credits to be eligible for Social Security benefits. In 2026, you earn one Social Security and Medicare credit for every $1,890 in covered earnings each year.
candidate_rules.source_title: Benefits Planner | Social Security Credits and Benefit Eligibility | SSA
candidate_rules.statement: To be eligible for Social Security retirement benefits, a worker must earn at least 40 Social Security credits (equivalent to approximately 10 years of work) by paying Social Security taxes. In 2026, one credit is earned for every $1,890 in covered earnings, with a maximum of four credits per year.

candidate_rules.citation_text: You can start receiving your Social Security retirement benefits as early as age 62. However, you are entitled to full benefits only when you reach your full retirement age.
candidate_rules.source_title: Benefits Planner: Retirement | Retirement Age and Benefit Reduction | SSA
candidate_rules.statement: Social Security retirement benefits can begin as early as age 62, but full benefits are only paid at full retirement age. Delaying benefits past full retirement age up to age 70 increases the monthly benefit amount; early claiming reduces it.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Generally, you need 40 credits, 20 of which were earned in the last 10 years ending with the year your disability begins. This is called the 20/40 Rule.
candidate_rules.source_title: How Does Someone Become Eligible? | Disability Benefits | SSA
candidate_rules.statement: For Social Security disability benefits, a worker generally needs 40 credits with 20 earned in the last 10 years ending with the year disability begins (the 20/40 Rule). Younger workers may qualify with fewer credits.

candidate_rules.citation_text: SSI is generally for individuals who don't earn more than $2,073 from work each month.
candidate_rules.source_title: Who can get SSI | SSA
candidate_rules.statement: To qualify for SSI, an individual must be at least 65 years old, blind, or have a qualifying disability, AND have limited income and resources. SSI is generally for individuals who do not earn more than $2,073 from work each month (2026 figure).

candidate_rules.citation_text: be either a U.S. citizen or national, or a noncitizen in one of the certain alien classifications granted by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS); reside in one of the 50 States, the District of Columbia, or the Northern Mariana Islands
candidate_rules.source_title: Understanding Supplemental Security Income (SSI)-- SSI Overview
candidate_rules.statement: SSI recipients must be a U.S. citizen or national, or a noncitizen in certain alien classifications granted by DHS; must reside in one of the 50 states, DC, or the Northern Mariana Islands; and must not be absent from the U.S. for a full calendar month or 30 or more consecutive days.

candidate_rules.citation_text: you are not eligible to receive SSI for any full calendar month you are incarcerated... We will hold the retroactive payments until you contact SSA and provide proof that you are no longer a prisoner.
candidate_rules.source_title: Understanding Supplemental Security Income (SSI)-- SSI Eligibility
candidate_rules.statement: SSI recipients who are incarcerated in a correctional institution for a full calendar month are not eligible to receive SSI for that month. Retroactive payments due before incarceration are held until the individual provides proof of release.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The first $65 of earnings and one half of earnings over $65 received in a month... Income tax refunds. Home energy assistance.
candidate_rules.source_title: Understanding Supplemental Security Income (SSI)-- SSI Income
candidate_rules.statement: For SSI income calculation, the first $65 of monthly earned income and one-half of earnings above $65 are excluded from countable income. SSI does not count income tax refunds, SNAP benefits, home energy assistance, or need-based state/local assistance.

candidate_rules.citation_text: a lifetime limit of five years (60 months) on the amount of time a family with an adult can receive assistance funded with federal funds
candidate_rules.source_title: Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC) and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) - Overview | ASPE
candidate_rules.statement: TANF imposes a federal lifetime limit of 60 months (5 years) on the receipt of federally funded cash assistance for families that include an adult recipient. States may set shorter time limits.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Provide assistance to needy families so that children may be cared for in their own homes... End the dependence of needy parents on government benefits by promoting job preparation, work, and marriage
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 45 CFR Part 260 -- General Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) Provisions
candidate_rules.statement: TANF is a block grant program under which states have broad flexibility to design their own programs and determine eligibility rules, benefit levels, and services, subject to four statutory purposes: (1) assist needy families; (2) end dependence through work; (3) prevent out-of-wedlock pregnancies; (4) encourage two-parent families.

candidate_rules.citation_text: States carry out their own programs and decide on things like... Rules for determining who qualifies for benefits.
candidate_rules.source_title: What is TANF? | HHS.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Each state or tribal territory sets its own TANF eligibility requirements. Applicants must be residents of the state where they apply. States cannot discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, disability, age, or sex in administering TANF.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The Federal-State Unemployment Insurance Program provides unemployment benefits to eligible workers who are unemployed through no fault of their own (as determined under state law), and meet other eligibility requirements of state
candidate_rules.source_title: How Do I File for Unemployment Insurance? | U.S. Department of Labor
candidate_rules.statement: Unemployment Insurance is a joint federal-state program. To qualify, workers must generally be unemployed through no fault of their own, meet state-specific earnings and work history requirements, and be able and available to work. Each state administers its own program following federal guidelines.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Most states require that you file for unemployment insurance (UI) benefits in the state where you performed the work, even if your employer is located in a different state.
candidate_rules.source_title: Initial application instructions | U.S. Department of Labor
candidate_rules.statement: Workers must generally file for unemployment insurance benefits in the state where they performed the work, even if their employer is located in a different state. Most states allow filing online or by phone.

candidate_rules.citation_text: To claim the EITC, you must be a U.S. citizen or resident alien all year.
candidate_rules.source_title: Who Qualifies for the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: To claim the EITC, you must be a U.S. citizen or resident alien all year; if you were a nonresident alien for any part of the tax year, you can only claim the EITC if your filing status is married filing jointly and your spouse is a U.S. citizen or resident alien.

candidate_rules.citation_text: To qualify for the EITC, you, your spouse if filing jointly, and the child claimed must have a valid Social Security number (SSN) issued on or before the due date of the tax return (including extensions).
candidate_rules.source_title: Who Qualifies for the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: To qualify for the EITC, you, your spouse if filing jointly, and the child claimed must have a valid Social Security number (SSN) issued on or before the due date of the tax return (including extensions).

candidate_rules.citation_text: Taxpayers without qualifying children may claim the EITC...only if they are between the ages of 25 and 64.
candidate_rules.source_title: Restructure the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) to Make It Simpler | National Taxpayer Advocate Annual Report 2024
candidate_rules.statement: Taxpayers without qualifying children may claim the EITC (childless EITC) only if they are between the ages of 25 and 64; investment income disqualifies a taxpayer if it exceeds $11,600 for tax year 2024.

candidate_rules.citation_text: By law, we must wait until mid-February to issue refunds to taxpayers who claim the Earned Income Tax Credit.
candidate_rules.source_title: Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: By law, the IRS must wait until mid-February to issue refunds to taxpayers who claim the Earned Income Tax Credit.

candidate_rules.citation_text: To get the EITC, qualified workers must file a tax return and claim the credit.
candidate_rules.source_title: Low to moderate income workers may be eligible for the Earned Income Tax Credit | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: To get the EITC, qualified workers must file a tax return and claim the credit, even if their earnings were below the income requirement to file.

candidate_rules.citation_text: update and define exceptions from the ABAWD time limit; and adjust the number of discretionary exemptions available to state agencies each year.
candidate_rules.source_title: Final Rule - SNAP: Program Purpose and Work Requirement Provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 | Food and Nutrition Service
candidate_rules.statement: SNAP able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWDs) are subject to a time limit on benefits; the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 updated and defined exceptions from the ABAWD time limit and adjusted the number of discretionary exemptions available to state agencies to 8% of the state's caseload ineligible due to the ABAWD time limit for FY 2024 and each subsequent fiscal year.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The final rule amends SNAP regulations for calculating standard utility allowances (SUAs) and expands allowable shelter expenses to include basic internet costs.
candidate_rules.source_title: SNAP - Implementation of Regulatory Changes to Standard Utility Allowances | Food and Nutrition Service
candidate_rules.statement: SNAP regulations for calculating standard utility allowances (SUAs) were amended by a final rule effective January 17, 2025, to expand allowable shelter expenses to include basic internet costs and to require state agencies to give the heating and cooling standard utility allowance (HCSUA) to households that incur any heating and cooling expenses, even if those costs are minimal.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Under section 9(b), the income limit for reduced-price school meals is 185 percent of the Federal poverty guidelines, as adjusted.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: WIC 2024/2025 Income Eligibility Guidelines
candidate_rules.statement: Persons are income-eligible for WIC if they are members of families whose income satisfies the income standard prescribed for reduced-price school meals under section 9(b) of the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act, which sets the income limit at 185 percent of the federal poverty guidelines, as adjusted annually.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Women who are currently pregnant, postpartum (up to 6 months after the end of a pregnancy), or breastfeeding (up to the infant's first birthday)
candidate_rules.source_title: WIC Eligibility | Food and Nutrition Administration
candidate_rules.statement: WIC categorical eligibility is limited to women who are currently pregnant, postpartum (up to 6 months after the end of a pregnancy), or breastfeeding (up to the infant's first birthday), and infants and children up to age five who are at nutritional risk. Applicants receiving Medicaid, SNAP, or TANF may already be income eligible for WIC.

candidate_rules.citation_text: All applicants must receive a free, simple health check by WIC staff before they are enrolled.
candidate_rules.source_title: WIC Eligibility | Food and Nutrition Administration
candidate_rules.statement: All WIC applicants must receive a free, simple health check by WIC staff before they are enrolled; physical presence at each certification or recertification is required under 7 CFR 246.7(o)(1), though ARPA waivers allow state agencies to offer remote certification options.

candidate_rules.citation_text: This rule is effective June 17, 2024.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: WIC Revisions in the WIC Food Packages (Final Rule, April 18, 2024)
candidate_rules.statement: WIC food packages were revised by a final rule effective June 17, 2024, to align with the 2020-2025 Dietary Guidelines for Americans and NASEM recommendations, providing WIC participants with a wider variety of foods and giving state agencies greater flexibility to tailor food packages to participants' dietary needs and cultural food preferences.

candidate_rules.citation_text: These eligibility guidelines are based on the Federal income poverty guidelines and are stated by household size.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: Child Nutrition Programs: Income Eligibility Guidelines (2025-2026)
candidate_rules.statement: Children from families with incomes at or below 130 percent of the federal poverty level are eligible for free school meals; those with incomes between 130 percent and 185 percent of the poverty level are eligible for reduced-price meals. Income eligibility guidelines are issued annually by USDA and are based on the federal income poverty guidelines stated by household size.

candidate_rules.citation_text: If you receive Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits, all of your children who attend school automatically qualify for free school meals.
candidate_rules.source_title: Families/Caregivers | Food and Nutrition Service (NSLP)
candidate_rules.statement: If a household receives SNAP benefits, all children in that household who attend school automatically qualify for free school meals. Participation in TANF also provides automatic eligibility for free school meals.

candidate_rules.citation_text: school food authorities certified as meeting the meal pattern and nutrition standard requirements...are eligible to receive performance-based cash assistance for each reimbursable lunch served
candidate_rules.source_title: National School Lunch, Special Milk, and School Breakfast Programs, National Average Payments/Maximum Reimbursement Rates SY 2025-26 | Food and Nutrition Administration
candidate_rules.statement: School food authorities certified as meeting the meal pattern and nutrition standard requirements set forth in 7 CFR parts 210 and 220 are eligible to receive performance-based cash assistance for each reimbursable lunch served (an additional nine cents per lunch beginning July 1, 2024, adjusted annually thereafter).

candidate_rules.citation_text: No later than February 1, 2013, and by February 1st each year thereafter, each State agency must collect annual verification data from each local educational agency
candidate_rules.source_title: Interim Final Rule: National School Lunch Program and School Breakfast Program: Elimination of the State Ameliorative Action Reporting Requirement | Food and Nutrition Service
candidate_rules.statement: Each year, school districts must verify a sample of applications for free or reduced-price school meals for certification error. State agencies must collect annual verification data from each local educational agency by February 1 each year and report to FNS by March 15 each year.

candidate_rules.citation_text: This eligibility criteria must include maximum income-based standards at or between 185 percent to 300 percent of the U.S. Federal Poverty Guidelines
candidate_rules.source_title: TEFAP Income Guidelines | Food and Nutrition Service
candidate_rules.statement: TEFAP is a federal program that helps supplement the diets of low-income people by providing emergency food assistance at no cost. Households must meet state-established eligibility criteria; each state sets income standards for home consumption eligibility, which per 7 CFR 251.5(b) must be set at or between 185 percent and 300 percent of the U.S. Federal Poverty Guidelines.

candidate_rules.citation_text: TEFAP regulations do not require that applicant households provide verification of income eligibility such as pay stubs.
candidate_rules.source_title: Participant Eligibility in TEFAP (Revised) | Food and Nutrition Service
candidate_rules.statement: TEFAP regulations do not require that applicant households provide verification of income eligibility such as pay stubs; a state agency may choose whether to require verification and determine the process. Self-attestation of income is an allowable practice.

candidate_rules.citation_text: All ERAs must meet minimum requirements outlined in program regulations; for example, those that provide prepared meals must demonstrate that they predominately serve people with low-income.
candidate_rules.source_title: TEFAP Factsheet | Food and Nutrition Service
candidate_rules.statement: Public or private nonprofit organizations that provide nutrition assistance to low-income people, by providing prepared meals or food for use at home, may be eligible to distribute USDA Foods through TEFAP as eligible recipient agencies (ERAs). All ERAs must meet minimum requirements outlined in program regulations at 7 CFR Parts 250 and 251; those providing prepared meals must demonstrate that they predominantly serve people with low income.

candidate_rules.citation_text: For meals that local organizations prepare and serve in a group setting, you do not have to meet a certain income level because these organizations have already shown that they serve mostly low-income people.
candidate_rules.source_title: TEFAP Applicant/Recipient | Food and Nutrition Administration
candidate_rules.statement: For TEFAP meals served in a group setting (e.g., soup kitchens), individual households do not have to meet an income threshold because the serving organization has already demonstrated that it predominantly serves low-income people. For home consumption, income eligibility is required and determined by the state.

candidate_rules.citation_text: In general, the family's income may not exceed 50% of the median income for the county or metropolitan area in which the family chooses to live.
candidate_rules.source_title: Housing Choice Voucher Program Section 8 | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: A family's annual income may not exceed 50% of the median income for the county or metropolitan area in which the family chooses to live; by law, a PHA must provide 75% of its vouchers to applicants whose incomes do not exceed 30% of the area median income.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Applicants must be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen as defined by HUD. The head of the household must have a valid Social Security number.
candidate_rules.source_title: Housing Choice Voucher Tenants | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Applicants must be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen as defined by HUD, and the head of household must have a valid Social Security number.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Regulations are found in 24 CFR Part 982.
candidate_rules.source_title: Housing Choice Voucher Program Section 8 | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: HCV program regulations are codified at 24 CFR Part 982.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The PHA determines a payment standard that is the amount generally needed to rent a moderately-priced dwelling unit in the local housing market.
candidate_rules.source_title: Housing Choice Voucher Program Section 8 | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: The PHA determines a payment standard representing the amount generally needed to rent a moderately-priced dwelling unit in the local housing market, which is used to calculate the amount of housing assistance a family will receive.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Those new voucher-holders not living in the jurisdiction of the PHA at the time the family applied for housing assistance must initially lease a unit within that jurisdiction for the first twelve months of assistance.
candidate_rules.source_title: Housing Choice Voucher Program Section 8 | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: New voucher-holders not living in the jurisdiction of the issuing PHA at the time of application must initially lease a unit within that jurisdiction for the first twelve months of assistance.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The PHA will verify this information with other local agencies, your employer and bank, and will use the information to determine program eligibility and the amount of the housing assistance payment.
candidate_rules.source_title: Housing Choice Voucher Program Section 8 | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: The PHA will verify family income, assets, and composition with local agencies, employers, and banks to determine program eligibility and the amount of housing assistance payment.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The housing unit selected by the family must meet an acceptable level of health and safety before the PHA can approve the unit.
candidate_rules.source_title: Housing Choice Voucher Program Section 8 | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: The housing unit selected by the family must meet an acceptable level of health and safety before the PHA can approve the unit; the PHA must inspect the dwelling and determine that the rent requested is reasonable.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Each PHA must ensure that 75 percent of its admissions in each PHA fiscal year are families whose incomes are at or below the extremely low-income (ELI) limit.
candidate_rules.source_title: HCV Guidebook: Eligibility Determination and Denial of Assistance, November 2019 | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Each PHA must ensure that 75% of its admissions in each PHA fiscal year are families whose incomes are at or below the extremely low-income (ELI) limit; less than 75% ELI is permitted only with HUD approval.

candidate_rules.citation_text: If your income or household members change (persons move in or out of your home), you must notify your housing agency.
candidate_rules.source_title: Housing Choice Voucher Tenants | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Participants must notify their housing agency if income or household members change; for adding any household member other than by birth, adoption, or court-awarded custody, PHA approval is required.

candidate_rules.citation_text: An HA determines your eligibility based on: 1) annual gross income; 2) whether you qualify as elderly, a person with a disability, or as a family; and 3) U.S. citizenship.
candidate_rules.source_title: Public Housing Program | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Public housing eligibility is limited to low-income families and individuals; an HA determines eligibility based on annual gross income, whether the applicant qualifies as elderly, a person with a disability, or as a family, and U.S. citizenship or eligible immigration status.

candidate_rules.citation_text: HUD sets the lower income limits at 80% and very low-income limits at 50% of the median income for the county or metropolitan area in which you choose to live.
candidate_rules.source_title: Public Housing Program | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: HUD sets lower income limits at 80% and very low-income limits at 50% of the median income for the county or metropolitan area; income limits vary by area.

candidate_rules.citation_text: No family other than a low income family is eligible for admission to a PHA's public housing program.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 24 CFR Part 960 -- Admission to, and Occupancy of, Public Housing
candidate_rules.statement: No family other than a low income family is eligible for admission to a PHA's public housing program, per 24 CFR Part 960.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The PHA must affirmatively further fair housing in the administration of its public housing program.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 24 CFR Part 960 -- Admission to, and Occupancy of, Public Housing
candidate_rules.statement: The PHA must affirmatively further fair housing in the administration of its public housing program, per 24 CFR Part 960.

candidate_rules.citation_text: If it is determined that you are ineligible, the HA must say why and, if you wish, you can request an informal hearing.
candidate_rules.source_title: Public Housing Program | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: If an HA determines an applicant is ineligible for public housing, the HA must state the reason in writing, and the applicant may request an informal hearing.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The family must supply any information that the PHA or HUD determines is necessary in administration of the public housing program, including submission of required evidence of citizenship or eligible immigration status.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 24 CFR Part 960 -- Admission to, and Occupancy of, Public Housing
candidate_rules.statement: The family must supply any information that the PHA or HUD determines is necessary in administration of the public housing program, including submission of required evidence of citizenship or eligible immigration status, per 24 CFR Part 960.

candidate_rules.citation_text: PHAs must send a formal notice of denial to an applicant who is denied admission.
candidate_rules.source_title: Eligibility Determination and Denial of Assistance (Public Housing) | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: PHAs must send a formal notice of denial to an applicant who is denied admission; if denied due to criminal activity, the notice must offer the applicant a copy of the criminal records and an opportunity to dispute them.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The LIHEAP statute establishes 150 percent of the poverty level as the maximum income level allowed in determining LIHEAP income eligibility, except where 60 percent of state median income is higher.
candidate_rules.source_title: LIHEAP Service Eligibility Guidelines | The Administration for Children and Families
candidate_rules.statement: The LIHEAP statute establishes the maximum income level for eligibility as the greater of 150% of the federal poverty level or 60% of a State's median income; income eligibility criteria may not be set lower than 110% of the poverty level.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Grant recipients may not exclude from eligibility solely on the basis of household income which falls below 110 percent of FPG for such State.
candidate_rules.source_title: LIHEAP IM 2023-01 Federal Poverty Guidelines for Optional Use in FFY 2023 and Mandatory Use in FFY 2024 | ACF
candidate_rules.statement: LIHEAP grant recipients may make eligible solely on the basis of household income which does not exceed the greater of 150% of FPG for the State or 60% of the State Median Income (SMI); grant recipients may not exclude from eligibility solely on the basis of income households with incomes below 110% of FPG.

candidate_rules.citation_text: In order to be eligible for LIHEAP, most states require that an applicant household prove it has an obligation or responsibility to pay its home energy bill.
candidate_rules.source_title: Eligibility | The LIHEAP Clearinghouse
candidate_rules.statement: In order to be eligible for LIHEAP, most grantees require that an applicant household prove it has an obligation or responsibility to pay its home energy bill (energy burden), reflected through an active account with a utility or fuel vendor, a current energy bill, and evidence that the household pays the vendor directly.

candidate_rules.citation_text: tenants described in subsection (a)(2) who are responsible for paying some or all heating or cooling costs shall not have their eligibility automatically denied.
candidate_rules.source_title: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) | HHS Guidance Portal
candidate_rules.statement: Tenants in subsidized housing who are responsible for paying some or all heating or cooling costs shall not have their LIHEAP eligibility automatically denied; however, the state may consider the amount of the heating or cooling component of utility allowances when setting benefit levels.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Since LIHEAP is a block-grant program, grant recipients have many options and flexibility for program design.
candidate_rules.source_title: LIHEAP Eligibility and Benefit Determinations | HHS/ACF
candidate_rules.statement: LIHEAP is a block-grant program; grants are provided by the Office of Community Services (OCS) in the Administration for Children and Families (ACF), and grant recipients have many options and flexibility for program design.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The HEARTH Act of 2009 consolidates three of the separate homeless assistance programs administered by HUD under the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act into a single grant program.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: Homeless Emergency Assistance and Rapid Transition to Housing: Continuum of Care Program
candidate_rules.statement: The McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act is the primary federal statute addressing homelessness; the HEARTH Act of 2009 consolidated three separate HUD homeless assistance programs into a single Continuum of Care grant program and renamed the Emergency Shelter Grants program as the Emergency Solutions Grants program.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The final rule provides four categories under which individuals and families may qualify as homeless.
candidate_rules.source_title: HUD Notice on Limitation on Use of Funds to Serve Persons (CoC/SHP) | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: HUD's final rule on the definition of homelessness (published December 5, 2011) provides four categories under which individuals and families may qualify as homeless; Category 1 covers individuals and families who lack a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Legal Authority: Subtitle C of Title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11381-11389). Regulations are at 24 CFR part 578.
candidate_rules.source_title: Programs of HUD | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: The Continuum of Care (CoC) program regulations are codified at 24 CFR Part 578, authorized under Subtitle C of Title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11381-11389).

candidate_rules.citation_text: For three of the four programs (ESG, S+C, and SHP), the McKinney-Vento Act imposes a requirement to match certain amounts provided through the McKinney-Vento grants with an equal amount of funds.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: Matching Requirement in McKinney-Vento Act Programs
candidate_rules.statement: For three McKinney-Vento programs (ESG, Shelter Plus Care, and Supportive Housing Program), the Act imposes a requirement to match certain grant amounts with an equal amount of funds from other sources.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Have not had a lease, ownership interest, or occupancy agreement in permanent housing at any time during the 60 days immediately preceding the date of application for homeless assistance.
candidate_rules.source_title: HUD Notice on Limitation on Use of Funds to Serve Persons (CoC/SHP) | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Applicants eligible for permanent supportive housing under CoC/SHP must come from homelessness as defined under the McKinney-Vento Act; unaccompanied youth under 25 or families with children qualifying under Category 3 must not have had a lease or ownership interest in permanent housing in the 60 days preceding application and must have experienced two or more moves in that period.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Division N, Section 501(c) of the Act requires that grantees use at least 90 percent of the funds to provide financial assistance such as the payment of rent, rental arrears, utilities and home energy costs.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: Emergency Rental Assistance (Treasury, January 2021)
candidate_rules.statement: Under the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (Division N, Section 501), grantees must use at least 90% of Emergency Rental Assistance funds to provide financial assistance for rent, rental arrears, utilities, and home energy costs; no more than 10% may be used for housing stability services and administrative costs.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Section 3201 of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, enacted March 11, 2021, appropriates additional funds for States, political subdivisions, and U.S. territories to provide financial assistance to households to pay rent, utilities, home energy expenses, and other related expenses.
candidate_rules.source_title: Emergency Rental Assistance Frequently Asked Questions | IRS
candidate_rules.statement: Under the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (Section 3201), additional Emergency Rental Assistance funds were appropriated for States, political subdivisions, and U.S. territories to provide financial assistance to households to pay rent, utilities, home energy expenses, and other related expenses.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Emergency Rental Assistance is intended to help eligible households that require financial assistance to pay for rent, utilities, home energy expenses, and other related expenses, and the payments are excluded from income only for those households.
candidate_rules.source_title: Emergency Rental Assistance Frequently Asked Questions | IRS
candidate_rules.statement: Emergency Rental Assistance payments are excluded from income only for eligible households that require financial assistance to pay for rent, utilities, home energy expenses, and other related expenses; rental payments received by landlords are includible in gross income.

candidate_rules.citation_text: In general, people who wish to apply for the EHV program must be referred to a PHA by a Continuum of Care (CoC).
candidate_rules.source_title: Emergency Housing Vouchers (EHVs) For USDA Rural Development Properties | HUD.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Emergency Housing Voucher (EHV) applicants must be referred to a PHA by a Continuum of Care (CoC), which verifies the person or family meets eligibility criteria before referral; EHV assistance is administered under HCV regulations at 24 CFR Part 982 except where HUD has established alternative requirements.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Each state has its own eligibility rules.
candidate_rules.source_title: Get emergency rent assistance | USAGov
candidate_rules.statement: Each state has its own eligibility rules for emergency rental assistance; applicants should contact their state or local agency, which may refer them to a community or nonprofit organization if they do not qualify for a government program.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Most U.S. citizens and permanent residents who work in the United States need to file a tax return if they make more than a certain amount for the year.
candidate_rules.source_title: Here's who needs to file a tax return in 2024 | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Most U.S. citizens and permanent residents who work in the United States need to file a federal income tax return if they make more than a certain threshold amount for the year, which varies by filing status.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Gross income means all income a person received in the form of money, goods, property and services that aren't exempt from tax.
candidate_rules.source_title: Here's who needs to file a tax return in 2024 | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Gross income means all income a person received in the form of money, goods, property and services that are not exempt from tax, including income from sources outside the United States or from the sale of a main home.

candidate_rules.citation_text: When your income jumps to a higher tax bracket, you don't pay the higher rate on your entire income.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal income tax rates and brackets | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Federal income tax is structured in progressive tax brackets; taxpayers pay tax as a percentage of income in layers, and when income jumps to a higher bracket, the higher rate applies only to the portion in the new bracket, not the entire income.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Congress typically enacts Federal tax law in the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (IRC).
candidate_rules.source_title: Tax code, regulations and official guidance | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Congress enacts federal tax law in the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (IRC), found in Title 26 of the United States Code (26 USC); Treasury regulations provide the official interpretation of the IRC and are found in Title 26 of the Code of Federal Regulations (26 CFR).

candidate_rules.citation_text: Self-employed individuals must file an annual return and pay estimated tax quarterly if they had net earnings from self-employment of $400 or more.
candidate_rules.source_title: Here's who needs to file a tax return in 2024 | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Self-employed individuals must file an annual return and pay estimated tax quarterly if they had net earnings from self-employment of $400 or more.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The amount of state and local income tax you pay will depend on how much income you earn and the tax rate of the state or locality where you live.
candidate_rules.source_title: How to pay and get help with state and local taxes | USAGov
candidate_rules.statement: The amount of state and local income tax a taxpayer pays depends on how much income they earn and the tax rate of the state or locality where they live; taxpayers should contact their state's tax agency for specific rules and forms.

candidate_rules.citation_text: You may deduct as an itemized deduction, state and local income taxes withheld from your wages during the year (as reported on your Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement).
candidate_rules.source_title: Topic no. 503, Deductible taxes | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Taxpayers may deduct state and local income taxes withheld from wages (as reported on Form W-2) and estimated or prior-year state and local income taxes paid during the year as an itemized deduction on Schedule A of Form 1040, subject to the SALT cap.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The current tax rate for Social Security is 6.2% for the employer and 6.2% for the employee, or 12.4% total.
candidate_rules.source_title: Topic no. 751, Social Security and Medicare withholding rates | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: FICA taxes are composed of Social Security taxes (6.2% employer + 6.2% employee = 12.4% total) and Medicare taxes (1.45% employer + 1.45% employee = 2.9% total); only Social Security tax has a wage base limit ($184,500 for 2026); all covered wages are subject to Medicare tax.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Employers are responsible for withholding the 0.9% Additional Medicare tax on an individual's wages paid in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year, without regard to filing status.
candidate_rules.source_title: Topic no. 751, Social Security and Medicare withholding rates | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Employers are responsible for withholding the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on an individual's wages paid in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year, without regard to filing status; there is no employer match for Additional Medicare Tax.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Generally, employers must report wages, tips and other compensation paid to an employee by filing the required form(s) to the IRS.
candidate_rules.source_title: Depositing and reporting employment taxes | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Employers must generally report wages, tips, and other compensation paid to employees by filing required employment tax returns (Forms 940, 941, 943, 944, 945) and must deposit federal income tax and Additional Medicare Tax withheld, plus both employer and employee Social Security and Medicare taxes, using either a monthly or semi-weekly deposit schedule.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Deposits for FUTA Tax (Form 940) are required for the quarter within which the tax due exceeds $500.
candidate_rules.source_title: Depositing and reporting employment taxes | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Federal tax deposits must be made by electronic funds transfer (EFT); FUTA tax deposits are required for any quarter in which the tax due exceeds $500, and must be deposited by the end of the month following the end of that quarter.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The self-employment tax rate is 15.3%. The rate consists of two parts: 12.4% for social security and 2.9% for Medicare.
candidate_rules.source_title: Self-employment tax (Social Security and Medicare taxes) | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: The self-employment tax rate is 15.3% (12.4% for Social Security and 2.9% for Medicare); self-employed individuals calculate SE tax using Schedule SE (Form 1040) and may deduct the employer-equivalent portion of SE tax in computing adjusted gross income.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The sales tax you pay is based on a percentage of the sales price of an item you buy.
candidate_rules.source_title: How to pay and get help with state and local taxes | USAGov
candidate_rules.statement: Sales tax is based on a percentage of the sales price of an item purchased; most states and municipalities have a sales tax and charge different percentages on different goods, or not at all for other items; sales tax rules are set at the state and local level.

candidate_rules.citation_text: As an individual, your deduction for state and local taxes (SALT) is limited to a combined total deduction of $40,000 ($20,000 if married filing separately).
candidate_rules.source_title: Topic no. 503, Deductible taxes | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Taxpayers who itemize deductions may elect to deduct state and local general sales taxes in lieu of state and local income taxes on Schedule A (Form 1040); the total SALT deduction (income, sales, and property taxes combined) is capped at $40,000 ($20,000 if married filing separately), subject to a modified AGI limitation but not reduced below $10,000.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Your local government's taxes your land, home, or other immovable assets. The amount you pay can depend on the market value, location, and condition.
candidate_rules.source_title: How to pay and get help with state and local taxes | USAGov
candidate_rules.statement: Real estate (property) tax is levied by local governments on land, homes, or other immovable assets; the amount owed can depend on the market value, location, and condition of the property, and is generally paid to the local government.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Deductible real property taxes are generally any state or local taxes on real property levied for the general public welfare.
candidate_rules.source_title: Topic no. 503, Deductible taxes | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Deductible real property taxes are generally any state or local taxes on real property levied for the general public welfare; the charge must be uniform against all real property in the jurisdiction at a like rate; taxpayers must have paid them at settlement, closing, or to a taxing authority during the year.

candidate_rules.citation_text: You can't deduct amounts you pay for local benefits that tend to increase the value of your property.
candidate_rules.source_title: Publication 530 (2025), Tax Information for Homeowners | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: Taxpayers cannot deduct amounts paid for local benefits that tend to increase the value of their property (e.g., construction of streets, sidewalks, or water/sewer systems); they must add these amounts to the basis of the property. However, assessments for maintenance, repair, or interest charges related to those benefits are deductible.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The overall limit on the deduction for state and local income, sales, and property tax has increased to $40,000 ($20,000 if married filing separately).
candidate_rules.source_title: Publication 530 (2025), Tax Information for Homeowners | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: The overall SALT deduction limit for state and local income, sales, and property taxes has increased to $40,000 ($20,000 if married filing separately), reduced if modified AGI exceeds $500,000 ($250,000 if married filing separately) but not below $10,000 ($5,000 if married filing separately).

candidate_rules.citation_text: A refundable tax credit is a credit you can get as a refund even if you don't owe any tax.
candidate_rules.source_title: Refundable tax credits | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: A refundable tax credit is a credit you can get as a refund even if you don't owe any tax; refundable credits go beyond reducing tax to zero and give any remaining credit as a refund.

candidate_rules.citation_text: You can't get a credit or refund if you don't file the claim within 3 years of filing your original return, or 2 years after paying the tax, whichever is later.
candidate_rules.source_title: Time you can claim a credit or refund | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: A taxpayer cannot get a credit or refund if the claim is not filed within 3 years of filing the original return, or 2 years after paying the tax, whichever is later, unless an exception applies; this period is called the Refund Statute Expiration Date (RSED).

candidate_rules.citation_text: To qualify, you must have under $11,950 in investment income and earn less than a specific income level from working.
candidate_rules.source_title: Refundable tax credits | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: For 2025, the Earned Income Tax Credit requires investment income under $11,950 and earned income below a specific level ranging from $19,104 (single, no children) to $68,675 (married filing jointly, 3+ children).

candidate_rules.citation_text: If a taxpayer's tax bill is less than the amount of a refundable credit, they can get the difference back in their refund.
candidate_rules.source_title: Tax credits for individuals: What they mean and how they can help refunds | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: If a taxpayer's tax bill is less than the amount of a refundable credit, they can get the difference back in their refund; nonrefundable credits cannot reduce tax below zero.

candidate_rules.citation_text: If you claim a refund or credit on your federal tax return of more than $2 million ($5 million for a C corporation), the IRS must review the refund or credit and provide a report to the Joint Committee on Taxation.
candidate_rules.source_title: Large tax refunds and credits subject to review by the Joint Committee on Taxation | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: If a refund or credit on a federal tax return exceeds $2 million ($5 million for a C corporation), the IRS must review it and provide a report to the Joint Committee on Taxation before it is paid.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Earned Income Credit claim - By law, refunds on tax returns that include this credit are held until mid-February to prevent fraud.
candidate_rules.source_title: Refunds | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: By law, refunds on tax returns that include an Earned Income Credit claim are held until mid-February to prevent fraud.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Existing Treasury Regulations require that for a claim for refund to be valid, it must set forth sufficient facts to apprise the IRS of the basis of the claim.
candidate_rules.source_title: Required information for a valid research credit claim for refund | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: For a research credit (IRC Section 41) claim for refund to be valid, Treasury Regulations require it to set forth sufficient facts to apprise the IRS of the basis of the claim, including total qualified employee wage expenses, supply expenses, and contract research expenses.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Are affected by a Presidentially declared disaster: You may have up to 1 more year to claim a credit or refund.
candidate_rules.source_title: Time you can claim a credit or refund | Internal Revenue Service
candidate_rules.statement: A taxpayer affected by a Presidentially declared disaster may have up to 1 additional year beyond the standard RSED to claim a credit or refund; a taxpayer serving in a designated combat zone may also qualify for additional time.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The term 'licensure' generally refers to an official process, administered by a state-level authority, that is required by law in order for an individual to practice a regulated profession.
candidate_rules.source_title: Professional Licensure | U.S. Department of Education
candidate_rules.statement: Regulated professions in the United States are generally licensed at the state level; 'licensure' refers to an official process administered by a state-level authority required by law for an individual to practice a regulated profession.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Most licensed professions require some formal postsecondary education or training as a prerequisite for entry.
candidate_rules.source_title: Professional Licensure | U.S. Department of Education
candidate_rules.statement: The competent authority for recognizing professional qualifications is generally the appropriate state or territorial licensing authority in the jurisdiction where one intends to work; most licensed professions require some formal postsecondary education or training as a prerequisite for entry.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Under the updated law, a covered servicemember or spouse's out-of-state license must be considered valid for the scope of practice in the state of the new residence.
candidate_rules.source_title: Servicemembers and Veterans Initiative | Professional License Portability | U.S. Department of Justice
candidate_rules.statement: Under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA) as amended in December 2024, a covered servicemember or spouse's out-of-state professional license must be considered valid for the scope of practice in the state of the new residence when relocating due to military orders; all professional licenses including law licenses are eligible for portability.

candidate_rules.citation_text: When a servicemember or spouse applies for SCRA license portability, anything demanded in excess of the requirements detailed in the SCRA is illegal.
candidate_rules.source_title: Servicemembers and Veterans Initiative | Professional License Portability | U.S. Department of Justice
candidate_rules.statement: When a servicemember or spouse applies for SCRA license portability, the licensing authority may only request the three items specified in the SCRA; anything demanded in excess of those requirements is illegal, and the law does not permit requesting transcripts or test scores.

candidate_rules.citation_text: In most cases, you will not need a license to import goods into the U.S. But for some items, agencies may require a license, permit, or other certification.
candidate_rules.source_title: Small business | USAGov
candidate_rules.statement: In most cases, a license is not required to import goods into the U.S., but for some items, federal agencies may require a license, permit, or other certification; most items exported to a foreign buyer will not need an export license or permit, but all items are subject to export control laws and regulations.

candidate_rules.citation_text: You must obtain SBA's prior written approval for any proposed transfer or issuance of ownership interests that results in the ownership...of at least 10 percent of any class of your stock or partnership capital.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 13 CFR Part 107 Subpart D -- Changes in Ownership, Control, or Structure of Licensee; Transfer of License
candidate_rules.statement: Under 13 CFR Part 107, a Small Business Investment Company (SBIC) licensee must obtain SBA's prior written approval for any proposed transfer or issuance of ownership interests resulting in ownership of at least 10 percent of any class of stock or partnership capital; a processing fee of $200 must accompany each such request.

candidate_rules.citation_text: A DMV may issue a REAL ID driver's license or identification card only to a person who has presented satisfactory evidence of lawful status.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 6 CFR Part 37 -- Real ID Driver's Licenses and Identification Cards
candidate_rules.statement: Under 6 CFR Part 37, a DMV may issue a REAL ID driver's license or identification card only to a person who has presented satisfactory evidence of lawful status.

candidate_rules.citation_text: States must require holders of REAL ID driver's licenses and identification cards to renew their driver's licenses and identification cards with the State DMV in person, no less frequently than every sixteen years.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 6 CFR 37.25 -- Renewal of REAL ID driver's licenses and identification cards
candidate_rules.statement: Under 6 CFR 37.25, states must require holders of REAL ID driver's licenses and identification cards to renew in person with the State DMV no less frequently than every sixteen years; the DMV must take an updated photograph at each such renewal.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Each applicant must sign a declaration under penalty of perjury that the information presented on the application is true and correct, and the State must retain this declaration.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 6 CFR 37.11 -- Application and documents the applicant must provide
candidate_rules.statement: Under 6 CFR 37.11, each REAL ID applicant must sign a declaration under penalty of perjury that the information presented on the application is true and correct; the state must retain this declaration and the applicant must sign a new declaration when presenting new source documents on subsequent visits.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The rule also requires agencies to coordinate their plans with DHS, make the plans publicly available, and achieve full enforcement by May 5, 2027.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register :: Minimum Standards for Driver's Licenses and Identification Cards Acceptable by Federal Agencies for Official Purposes; Phased Approach for Card-Based Enforcement
candidate_rules.statement: Under the REAL ID phased enforcement rule (effective January 2025), federal agencies may implement card-based enforcement provisions through a phased enforcement plan after the May 7, 2025 deadline, but must achieve full enforcement by May 5, 2027, and must coordinate plans with DHS and make them publicly available.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Generally, the federal government has few code requirements and states may impose some requirements, but the most detailed code requirements are adopted and enforced at the local government level.
candidate_rules.source_title: Building Codes, Standards, and Regulations: Frequently Asked Questions (EPA/CRS)
candidate_rules.statement: Generally, the federal government has few building code requirements; states may impose some requirements, but the most detailed code requirements are adopted and enforced at the local government level; building departments at the state, local, tribal, or territorial level are most often responsible for adopting and enforcing building codes and standards.

candidate_rules.citation_text: FEMA requires homeowners to follow more flood-resistant design standards used in recent editions of model building codes...to qualify for flood insurance under the National Flood Insurance Program.
candidate_rules.source_title: Building Codes, Standards, and Regulations: Frequently Asked Questions (EPA/CRS)
candidate_rules.statement: FEMA requires homeowners to follow more flood-resistant design standards used in recent editions of model building codes compared with some older building codes in order to qualify for flood insurance under the National Flood Insurance Program.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The FPISC is responsible for leading ongoing government-wide efforts to modernize the Federal permitting and review process for major infrastructure projects.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register :: Agencies - Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council
candidate_rules.statement: The Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council (FPISC), established under Title XLI of the FAST Act (Public Law 114-94), is responsible for leading government-wide efforts to modernize the federal permitting and review process for major infrastructure projects.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Although EPA directly issues some permits, many jurisdictions – such as states, territories, tribal nations and municipalities – are approved to directly implement federal environmental permit programs on EPA's behalf.
candidate_rules.source_title: About EPA Permitting | US EPA
candidate_rules.statement: Environmental permit rules are codified under Title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations (40 CFR), and EPA directly issues some permits while many jurisdictions—states, territories, tribal nations, and municipalities—are approved to directly implement federal environmental permit programs on EPA's behalf through delegation, assumption, authorization, or primacy.

candidate_rules.citation_text: When entities other than EPA administer federal permit programs, their regulations must be at least as stringent as federal regulations.
candidate_rules.source_title: About EPA Permitting | US EPA
candidate_rules.statement: When entities other than EPA administer federal environmental permit programs, their regulations must be at least as stringent as federal regulations; states, territories, tribal nations, and municipalities may also have their own environmental regulations and permit programs based on their own legislation.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Under the CAA, applicable stationary sources are required to obtain operating permits, known as title V permits, from the source's respective air permitting authority.
candidate_rules.source_title: EPA Issues Title V Permitting Guidance to Ensure Certainty for American Businesses and Alleviate Permitting Backlogs | US EPA
candidate_rules.statement: Under the Clean Air Act (CAA), applicable stationary sources are required to obtain operating permits, known as Title V permits, from the source's respective air permitting authority; these permits must compile all applicable air quality requirements into a single, comprehensive permit and be renewed periodically, even if there are no significant changes to operations or requirements.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The Clean Water Act limits the length of NPDES permits to five years.
candidate_rules.source_title: NPDES Permit Basics | US EPA
candidate_rules.statement: The Clean Water Act limits the length of NPDES permits to five years; NPDES permits can be renewed (reissued) at any time after the permit holder applies, and can be administratively extended if the facility reapplies more than 180 days before the permit expires and the permitting authority does not renew the permit before its expiration date through no fault of the permittee.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Appeal EPA-issued permits or permits issued by state or local agencies that are issuing the permit on behalf of the EPA to the Environmental Appeals Board and the federal courts.
candidate_rules.source_title: Participate in the Permitting Process | US EPA
candidate_rules.statement: Under the NSR permit program, the public may appeal EPA-issued permits or permits issued by state or local agencies acting on behalf of EPA to the Environmental Appeals Board and the federal courts; appeal procedures for state-issued permits depend on the state in which the source is located.

candidate_rules.citation_text: 2 CFR Part 200 provides a government-wide framework for grants management that reduces administrative burden for non-federal entities receiving federal awards while reducing the risk of waste, fraud and abuse.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 2 CFR Part 200 -- Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards
candidate_rules.statement: 2 CFR Part 200 (Uniform Guidance) establishes uniform administrative requirements, cost principles, and audit requirements for all Federal awards to non-Federal entities, providing a government-wide framework for grants management that reduces administrative burden while reducing the risk of waste, fraud, and abuse; the 2024 revision applies to projects starting on or after October 1, 2024.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Agencies may only impose legally binding requirements on recipients and subrecipients through: (1) Notice and public comment procedures through an approved agency process.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 2 CFR Part 200 -- Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards
candidate_rules.statement: Federal agencies may only impose legally binding requirements on recipients and subrecipients through notice and public comment procedures through an approved agency process, as authorized by 2 CFR Part 200, other statutes, or regulations; for Federal awards made subject to this part, it takes precedence over any administrative requirements, program manuals, handbooks, and other non-regulatory materials that are inconsistent with its requirements.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Some of the topics covered were changes to threshold amounts, equipment and supplies, updates of definitions and acronyms, new reporting requirements on budget and program plans as well as program performance, modifications to the termination clause, and procurement policies.
candidate_rules.source_title: What's New in the 2024 Revision to 2 CFR Part 200 | US EPA
candidate_rules.statement: Under 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart E, allowable costs incurred by grant recipients are governed by established cost principles; the 2024 revision updated threshold amounts, equipment and supplies definitions, reporting requirements on budget and program plans, program performance, and procurement policies.
