candidate_rules.citation_text: States must use their own policies and procedures. (See 2 CFR 200.317) ... All other non-Federal entities, including subrecipients of a state, must have and follow written procurement procedures that reflect the procurement standards in part 200.
candidate_rules.source_title: 2 CFR Part 200 Overview for Grantees (HUD)
candidate_rules.statement: Under 2 CFR 200.317, states must use their own policies and procedures for procurement under federal awards passed through to them; all other non-Federal entities, including subrecipients of a state, must have and follow written procurement procedures that reflect the procurement standards in 2 CFR Part 200.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The terms and conditions of Federal awards (including this part) flow down to subawards to subrecipients unless a particular section of this part or the terms and conditions of the Federal award specifically indicate otherwise.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 2 CFR 200.101 -- Applicability
candidate_rules.statement: The terms and conditions of Federal awards, including this part (2 CFR 200), flow down to subawards to subrecipients unless a particular section or the terms and conditions of the Federal award specifically indicate otherwise; pass-through entities must comply with the requirements described in subpart D, §§ 200.331 through 200.333.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The pass-through entity is responsible for making case-by-case determinations to determine whether the entity receiving Federal funds is a subrecipient or a contractor.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 2 CFR 200.331 -- Subrecipient and contractor determinations
candidate_rules.statement: Pass-through entities are responsible for making case-by-case determinations to determine whether the entity receiving Federal funds is a subrecipient or a contractor; the substance of the relationship is more important than the form of the agreement in making this determination.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The contracting officer must have the authority to the maximum extent practicable and consistent with law, to determine the application of rules, regulations, and policies, on a specific contract.
candidate_rules.source_title: Part 1 - Federal Acquisition Regulations System | Acquisition.GOV
candidate_rules.statement: The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), codified at Title 48 CFR, outlines procurement policies and procedures used by members of the Acquisition Team; the contracting officer must have authority to the maximum extent practicable and consistent with law to determine the application of rules, regulations, and policies on a specific contract.

candidate_rules.citation_text: With respect to acquisitions covered by the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement or a Free Trade Agreement, contracting officers must submit synopses in sufficient time to permit their publication in the GPE not later than 60 days after award.
candidate_rules.source_title: Subpart 5.3 - Synopses of Contract Awards | Acquisition.GOV
candidate_rules.statement: Contracting officers must synopsize through the Government Point of Entry (GPE) contract awards that are covered by the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement or a Free Trade Agreement, or that are likely to result in the award of any subcontracts; for acquisitions covered by WTO GPA or FTAs, synopses must be submitted in sufficient time to permit publication not later than 60 days after award.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Contracting officers shall make information available on awards over $5.5 million (unless another dollar amount is specified in agency acquisition regulations) in sufficient time for the agency concerned to announce it by 5 p.m. Washington, DC, time on the day of award.
candidate_rules.source_title: Subpart 5.3 - Synopses of Contract Awards | Acquisition.GOV
candidate_rules.statement: Contracting officers shall make information available on awards over $5.5 million in sufficient time for the agency to announce it by 5 p.m. Washington, DC time on the day of award; agencies shall not release information on awards before the public release time of 5 p.m. Washington, DC time.

candidate_rules.citation_text: When a Federal agency excludes a person under Executive Order 12549 or Executive Order 12689 on or after August 25, 1995, the excluded person is also ineligible for Federal procurement transactions under the Federal Acquisition Regulations.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 2 CFR Part 180 -- OMB Guidelines to Agencies on Government-Wide Debarment and Suspension (Nonprocurement)
candidate_rules.statement: The System for Award Management (SAM.gov) Exclusions, maintained by GSA, is the authoritative list of persons excluded from Federal procurement and nonprocurement programs; when a Federal agency excludes a person under Executive Order 12549 or 12689, the excluded person is also ineligible for Federal procurement transactions under the FAR, and vice versa—exclusions under the FAR have a reciprocal effect on nonprocurement transactions.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Federal agency officials use SAM.gov Exclusions to determine whether to enter into a transaction with a person, as required under § 180.430.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 2 CFR Part 180 Subpart E -- System for Award Management (SAM.gov) Exclusions
candidate_rules.statement: Federal agency officials must use SAM.gov Exclusions to determine whether to enter into a transaction with a person; the SAM.gov Exclusions is a widely available source of the most current information about persons who are excluded or disqualified from covered transactions, and GSA maintains and disseminates this list.

candidate_rules.citation_text: An offeror must be registered at time of offer submission and at time of contract award but would not be required to be registered in between those two points in time.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register :: Federal Acquisition Regulation: Clarification of System for Award Management Preaward Registration Requirements
candidate_rules.statement: An offeror must be registered in SAM.gov at the time of offer submission and at the time of contract award; the FAR was amended (effective August 7, 2025) to clarify that offerors are not required to maintain continuous SAM registration between offer submission and contract award, but active registration is the anticipated normal state expected of offerors and contractors conducting business with the Federal Government.

candidate_rules.citation_text: SAM contains the electronic roster of debarred companies excluded from Federal procurement and non-procurement programs throughout the U.S. Government (unless otherwise noted) and from receiving Federal contracts or certain subcontracts and from certain types of Federal financial and nonfinancial assistance and benefits.
candidate_rules.source_title: OFCCP Debarred Companies | U.S. Department of Labor
candidate_rules.statement: SAM contains the electronic roster of debarred companies excluded from Federal procurement and nonprocurement programs throughout the U.S. Government and from receiving Federal contracts or certain subcontracts and from certain types of Federal financial and nonfinancial assistance and benefits; the SAM system combines data from the Central Contractor Registration, Federal Register, Online Representations and Certification Applications, and the Excluded Parties List System.

candidate_rules.citation_text: OMB is implementing changes throughout 2 CFR to modernize reporting by recipients of Federal grants by requiring Federal agencies to adopt standard data elements
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: Guidance for Grants and Agreements (2020)
candidate_rules.statement: Federal agencies must require recipients of federal grants to adopt standard data elements for information recipients are required to report, as part of modernizing reporting under 2 CFR.

candidate_rules.citation_text: All recipient and subrecipient financial management systems...must be sufficient to permit the preparation of reports required by the terms and conditions
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR: 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart D – Post Federal Award Requirements
candidate_rules.statement: All recipient and subrecipient financial management systems must be sufficient to permit the preparation of reports required by the terms and conditions of the Federal award, and must track expenditures to establish that funds have been used in accordance with Federal statutes, regulations, and award terms (2 CFR 200 Subpart D).

candidate_rules.citation_text: grant and cooperative agreement recipients are responsible for reporting on executive compensation, when applicable, and subrecipient awards equal to or exceeding $30,000 in Federal funding
candidate_rules.source_title: EPA: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act
candidate_rules.statement: Under 2 CFR Part 170 (FFATA), grant and cooperative agreement recipients are responsible for reporting on executive compensation (when applicable) and subrecipient awards equal to or exceeding $30,000 in Federal funding, filed by end of the month following the month in which the prime recipient awards any such subaward.

candidate_rules.citation_text: the recipient must establish and maintain effective internal controls over Federal awards that provide reasonable assurance that awards are being managed in compliance with Federal statutes
candidate_rules.source_title: DOL: 2 CFR 200 Frequently Asked Questions (January 15, 2025)
candidate_rules.statement: Recipients must establish and maintain effective internal controls over Federal awards that provide reasonable assurance that awards are being managed in compliance with Federal statutes, regulations, and the Federal award terms and conditions (2 CFR Part 200).

candidate_rules.citation_text: United States laws enacted by Congress, including those in the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), govern matters related to processing and issuance of visas
candidate_rules.source_title: State Dept: U.S. Visa Law & Policy – Applying for a Visa
candidate_rules.statement: United States laws enacted by Congress, including those in the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), govern matters related to processing and issuance of visas and travel to the United States, including entry and exit of all travelers across the nation's borders.

candidate_rules.citation_text: A visa does not guarantee entry into the United States. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officials at the port-of-entry have authority to permit or deny admission
candidate_rules.source_title: State Dept: Visitor Visa (travel.state.gov)
candidate_rules.statement: A citizen of a foreign country who seeks to travel to the United States generally must first obtain a U.S. visa, either a nonimmigrant visa for a temporary stay or an immigrant visa for permanent residence. A visa does not guarantee entry; DHS/CBP officials at the port-of-entry have authority to permit or deny admission.

candidate_rules.citation_text: An individual on a visitor visa (B1/B2) is not permitted to accept employment or work in the United States.
candidate_rules.source_title: State Dept: Visitor Visa (travel.state.gov)
candidate_rules.statement: An individual on a visitor visa (B1/B2) is not permitted to accept employment or work in the United States. Attempting to obtain a visa by willful misrepresentation of a material fact or fraud may result in permanent refusal of a visa or denial of entry.

candidate_rules.citation_text: All U.S. employers must properly complete Form I-9 for every individual they hire for employment in the United States. This includes citizens and aliens.
candidate_rules.source_title: USCIS: Employment Eligibility Verification (Form I-9)
candidate_rules.statement: All U.S. employers must properly complete Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification, for every individual they hire for employment in the United States, including citizens and aliens. Employers must examine documents to determine whether they reasonably appear to be genuine and relate to the employee.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Your employees must complete and sign Section 1 of Form I-9 no later than their first day of employment
candidate_rules.source_title: USCIS: Completing Section 1, Employee Information and Attestation
candidate_rules.statement: Employees must complete and sign Section 1 of Form I-9 no later than their first day of employment. Employers must complete Section 2 (Employer Review and Verification) within three business days after the employee's first day of employment.

candidate_rules.citation_text: An employee must present a document or combination of documents from List A...or one document from List B...and one document from List C...within three business days of the date work for pay begins
candidate_rules.source_title: USCIS Handbook for Employers M-274: Acceptable Documents for Verifying Employment Authorization and Identity
candidate_rules.statement: An employee must present a document or combination of documents from List A (showing both identity and employment authorization) or one document from List B (identity) and one from List C (employment authorization) within three business days of the date work for pay begins.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Whether or not an alien is authorized to work in the United States depends on the alien's immigration status or circumstances.
candidate_rules.source_title: USCIS Policy Manual Volume 10 Part A Chapter 2 – Eligibility Requirements
candidate_rules.statement: Whether or not an alien is authorized to work in the United States depends on the alien's immigration status or circumstances. The regulations outline three classes of eligibility: authorization for any employer, authorization for a specific employer, and authorization requiring USCIS approval (8 CFR 274a.12).

candidate_rules.citation_text: Be at least 18 years old at the time of filing Form N-400...Be a permanent resident (have a 'Green Card') for at least 5 years.
candidate_rules.source_title: USCIS: Naturalization Information
candidate_rules.statement: General requirements for naturalization include: being at least 18 years old at time of filing Form N-400; being a lawful permanent resident (Green Card holder) for at least 5 years; having lived for at least 3 months in the state or USCIS district where applying; and demonstrating continuous residence in the United States for at least 5 years immediately preceding the filing date.

candidate_rules.citation_text: to be eligible for naturalization, an alien must establish that he or she...
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR: 8 CFR Part 316 – General Requirements for Naturalization
candidate_rules.statement: Under 8 CFR Part 316, to be eligible for naturalization an alien must establish lawful permanent resident status, continuous residence, physical presence, and residence in the state or USCIS district where the application is filed for at least 3 months.

candidate_rules.citation_text: You may file Form N-400, Application for Naturalization, 90 calendar days before you complete your continuous residence requirement
candidate_rules.source_title: USCIS: Application for Naturalization (Form N-400)
candidate_rules.statement: An applicant may file Form N-400, Application for Naturalization, 90 calendar days before completing the continuous residence requirement if eligibility is based on being a lawful permanent resident for at least 5 years, or 3 years if married to a U.S. citizen. USCIS will deny the N-400 if filed more than 90 days prior to the anniversary date.

candidate_rules.citation_text: On October 20, 2025, USCIS began implementing the 2025 naturalization civics test.
candidate_rules.source_title: USAGov: Become a U.S. Citizen Through Naturalization
candidate_rules.statement: During the naturalization interview, a USCIS Officer will ask questions about the applicant's Form N-400 and background. The applicant must also take an English test (reading, writing, speaking) and a civics test, unless qualifying for an exemption or waiver. Applicants who filed Form N-400 on or after October 20, 2025 must take the 2025 civics test.

candidate_rules.citation_text: To apply for asylum in the U.S., you must be physically present in the U.S. To apply for asylum, you should file Form I-589...within 1 year of your last arrival in the United States
candidate_rules.source_title: USCIS: The Affirmative Asylum Process
candidate_rules.statement: To apply for asylum in the United States, an applicant must be physically present in the U.S. and must file Form I-589, Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal, within 1 year of last arrival in the United States, unless an exception applies. Legal provisions are codified at INA Section 208 and 8 CFR 208.

candidate_rules.citation_text: A decision should be made on your asylum application within 180 days after the date you filed your application unless there are exceptional circumstances.
candidate_rules.source_title: USCIS: Q&A Affirmative Asylum Eligibility and Applications
candidate_rules.statement: A decision should be made on an asylum application within 180 days after the date the application is filed, unless there are exceptional circumstances. Applicant-caused delays do not count toward the 180-day eligibility period for employment authorization (8 CFR 208).

candidate_rules.citation_text: An asylee may adjust status to a lawful permanent resident if the asylee meets the following four requirements: The asylee has been physically present in the United States for at least 1 year after being granted asylum.
candidate_rules.source_title: USCIS Policy Manual Volume 7 Part M Chapter 2 – Eligibility Requirements (Asylee Adjustment)
candidate_rules.statement: An asylee may adjust status to lawful permanent resident if: (1) physically present in the U.S. for at least 1 year after being granted asylum; (2) the principal asylee continues to meet the definition of a refugee; (3) the asylee has not firmly resettled in any foreign country; and (4) the asylee is admissible to the U.S. as an immigrant at the time of examination.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Effective May 29, 2026, we will reject pending Form I-589 asylum applications for aliens who do not timely pay the AAF.
candidate_rules.source_title: USCIS: Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal (Form I-589)
candidate_rules.statement: Effective May 29, 2026, DHS published an interim final rule (implementing H.R. 1) establishing that if an alien does not pay the Annual Asylum Fee (AAF) within 30 days of notification, USCIS will reject their pending asylum application and deny any pending Form I-765 for employment authorization.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The documents on List A show both identity and employment authorization. Employees presenting an acceptable List A document should not be asked to present any other document.
candidate_rules.source_title: Form I-9 Acceptable Documents | USCIS
candidate_rules.statement: Employees must provide documentation to their employers to show their identity and authorization to work; documents on List A show both identity and employment authorization, and employees presenting an acceptable List A document should not be asked to present any other document.

candidate_rules.citation_text: States must verify SSNs with the Social Security Administration (SSA) or through another method approved by DHS. In the event of a non-match, a State may use existing procedures to resolve non-matches.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 6 CFR 37.13 -- Document verification requirements.
candidate_rules.statement: Under REAL ID regulations (6 CFR 37.13), states must verify SSNs with the Social Security Administration (SSA) or through another DHS-approved method before issuing a REAL ID driver's license or identification card; in the event of a non-match, the DMV must not issue a REAL ID credential until the information verifies with SSA.

candidate_rules.citation_text: If the identification card does not contain a photograph, identifying information shall be included such as: name, date of birth, sex, height, color of eyes, and address.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 8 CFR 274a.2 -- Verification of identity and employment authorization.
candidate_rules.statement: Under 8 CFR 274a.2, employers must verify identity and employment authorization using Form I-9; if an identification card does not contain a photograph, it must include identifying information such as name, date of birth, sex, height, color of eyes, and address to be acceptable for identity verification.

candidate_rules.citation_text: HSPD-12 directs the use of a mandatory common Federal identification credential for access to all federally controlled facilities and information systems.
candidate_rules.source_title: Personal Identity Verification /Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 | SSA
candidate_rules.statement: HSPD-12 directs the use of a mandatory common Federal identification credential (PIV card) for access to all federally controlled facilities and information systems; the credential must be issued based on sound criteria for verifying an individual's identity and must be strongly resistant to identity fraud, tampering, counterfeiting, and terrorism.

candidate_rules.citation_text: For the school year 2025-26, the federal deadline to submit the FAFSA is June 30, 2026. For the school year 2026-27, the federal deadline to submit the FAFSA is June 30, 2027.
candidate_rules.source_title: Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) | USAGov
candidate_rules.statement: For the school year 2025-26, the federal deadline to submit the FAFSA is June 30, 2026; for the school year 2026-27, the federal deadline is June 30, 2027; students must submit their FAFSA application on time to be considered for federal student aid.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Have a valid Social Security Number... Be enrolled in an eligible program as a regular student seeking a degree or certificate. Maintain satisfactory academic progress.
candidate_rules.source_title: Am I eligible to receive financial aid? | fafsa.ed.gov
candidate_rules.statement: To be eligible for federal student aid via FAFSA, applicants must have a valid Social Security Number, have a high school diploma or GED, be enrolled in an eligible program as a regular student seeking a degree or certificate, maintain satisfactory academic progress, and not owe a refund on a federal student grant or be in default on a federal student loan.

candidate_rules.citation_text: A student's eligibility to receive a Pell Grant award may be limited by the statutory provision in section 401(d)(5) of the HEA that sets a lifetime Pell Grant eligibility limit of 12 semesters (or its equivalent).
candidate_rules.source_title: 2026–27 Federal Pell Grant Maximum and Minimum Award Amounts | Knowledge Center (FSA Partners)
candidate_rules.statement: For the 2026-27 award year, the maximum Federal Pell Grant award is $7,395 and the minimum is 10% of the maximum; a student's eligibility to receive a Pell Grant award may be limited by the statutory provision in HEA Section 401(d)(5), which sets a lifetime Pell Grant eligibility limit of 12 semesters (or its equivalent).

candidate_rules.citation_text: To receive a Pell Grant based on eligibility under the Special Rule, a student must be: The child of a parent or guardian who died in the line of duty while either (a) serving on active duty as a member of the U.S. Armed Forces on or after September 11, 2001; or (b) actively serving as and performing the duties of a public safety officer; and Less than 33 years old as of the January 1 prior to the award year.
candidate_rules.source_title: Student Eligibility for Pell Grants | 2025-2026 Federal Student Aid Handbook
candidate_rules.statement: Under the Special Rule in HEA Section 401(c), a student must be the child of a parent or guardian who died in the line of duty while serving on active duty as a member of the U.S. Armed Forces on or after September 11, 2001, or actively serving as a public safety officer, AND must be less than 33 years old as of January 1 prior to the award year, to receive a maximum Pell Grant regardless of their calculated SAI.

candidate_rules.citation_text: A student is ineligible to receive further Pell Grant funds if they have reached or exceeded the 600% limit... You must submit Pell Grant disbursement information to COD no later than 15 calendar days after making a disbursement or adjustment.
candidate_rules.source_title: Pell Grant Lifetime Eligibility Used (LEU) | 2025-2026 Federal Student Aid Handbook
candidate_rules.statement: A student is ineligible to receive further Pell Grant funds if they have reached or exceeded the 600% Lifetime Eligibility Used (LEU) limit; schools must submit Pell Grant disbursement information to COD no later than 15 calendar days after making a disbursement or adjustment, and failure to do so could result in the Department disallowing the disbursement.

candidate_rules.citation_text: To be eligible for Direct Loans, a student must be enrolled on at least a half-time basis at a school that participates in the Direct Loan Program, and students and parents must meet the general federal student aid eligibility requirements covered in Volume 1 of the Federal Student Aid Handbook.
candidate_rules.source_title: Student and Parent Eligibility for Direct Loans | 2025-2026 Federal Student Aid Handbook
candidate_rules.statement: To be eligible for Direct Loans, a student must be enrolled on at least a half-time basis at a school that participates in the Direct Loan Program, and students and parents must meet the general federal student aid eligibility requirements; financial need is not an eligibility requirement to receive a Direct Unsubsidized Loan.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Beginning with the 2026–27 award year, student borrowers will have a new lifetime maximum aggregate loan limit of $257,500... Once a borrower reaches the $257,500 lifetime maximum aggregate loan limit, the borrower will no longer be eligible to receive additional Title IV loans, even if the borrower's loans have been repaid, forgiven, or discharged.
candidate_rules.source_title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act NSLDS Eligibility Processing Updates | Knowledge Center (FSA Partners)
candidate_rules.statement: Beginning with the 2026-27 award year, student borrowers will have a new lifetime maximum aggregate loan limit of $257,500 (including Direct Loans and FFEL Program loans); once a borrower reaches this limit, they will no longer be eligible to receive additional Title IV loans, even if prior loans have been repaid, forgiven, or discharged.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The Working Families Tax Cuts Act simplifies and streamlines the current confusing patchwork of repayment plan options for future borrowers to two flexible options: a new Tiered Standard repayment plan for fixed monthly payments over a 10 to 25-year term, and a new income-driven plan called the Repayment Assistance Plan.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register :: Reimagining and Improving Student Education-Federal Student Loan Program Final Regulations
candidate_rules.statement: The Working Families Tax Cuts Act (P.L. 119-21) simplifies repayment to two options for future borrowers: a new Tiered Standard repayment plan for fixed monthly payments over a 10 to 25-year term, and a new income-driven Repayment Assistance Plan; confusing and outdated plans including ICR, PAYE, and SAVE are phased out.

candidate_rules.citation_text: You served at least 90 days on active duty (either all at once or with breaks in service) on or after September 11, 2001, or You received a Purple Heart on or after September 11, 2001, and were honorably discharged after any amount of service.
candidate_rules.source_title: Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) | Veterans Affairs
candidate_rules.statement: To be eligible for the Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33), a veteran must have served at least 90 days on active duty on or after September 11, 2001 (continuous or with breaks), OR received a Purple Heart on or after September 11, 2001 and been honorably discharged, OR served at least 30 continuous days on or after September 11, 2001 and been honorably discharged with a service-connected disability.

candidate_rules.citation_text: As of January 2026, all education beneficiaries, including Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (Chapter 35) students, must verify their enrollment each month to receive benefit payments.
candidate_rules.source_title: Education and Training - Veterans Benefits Administration | VA
candidate_rules.statement: As of January 2026, all VA education beneficiaries, including Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (Chapter 35) students, must verify their enrollment each month to receive benefit payments; Post-9/11 GI Bill recipients must verify enrollment monthly to keep receiving monthly housing allowance or kicker payments.

candidate_rules.citation_text: When a student submits the FAFSA form, they are automatically applying for aid from not only the federal government but also the state
candidate_rules.source_title: Types of Aid and Eligibility | Federal Student Aid - Financial Aid Toolkit
candidate_rules.statement: When a student submits the FAFSA form, they are automatically applying for aid from not only the federal government but also the state and—in many cases—the school(s) listed on the FAFSA form.

candidate_rules.citation_text: the state must authorize the institution by name to operate postsecondary educational programs
candidate_rules.source_title: Institutional Eligibility | 2025-2026 Federal Student Aid Handbook
candidate_rules.statement: There are two basic requirements for an institution to be considered legally authorized by a state for the purpose of Title IV program eligibility: (1) the state must authorize the institution by name to operate postsecondary educational programs; and (2) the state must have a process to review and act on complaints concerning the institution, including enforcing applicable state laws.

candidate_rules.citation_text: A non-Federal entity that expends $1,000,000 or more during the non-Federal entity's fiscal year in Federal awards must have a single or program-specific audit conducted
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 2 CFR 200.501 -- Audit requirements.
candidate_rules.statement: A non-Federal entity that expends $1,000,000 or more during the non-Federal entity's fiscal year in Federal awards must have a single or program-specific audit conducted for that year in accordance with the provisions of 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart F.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The audit must be conducted in accordance with GAGAS
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 2 CFR 200.514 -- Standards and scope of audit.
candidate_rules.statement: The audit must be conducted in accordance with GAGAS and must cover the entire operations of the auditee, or include a series of audits covering departments, agencies, and other organizational units that expended or otherwise administered Federal awards during the audit period.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The law requires agencies across the federal government to adjust their penalties for inflation not later than January 15 of every year.
candidate_rules.source_title: Civil Money Penalty Inflation Adjustments | U.S. Department of Labor
candidate_rules.statement: The Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act Improvements Act of 2015 requires agencies to adjust civil monetary penalties for inflation annually, not later than January 15 of every year.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The OIG may impose CMPs, assessments, and exclusions against individuals and entities that engage in fraud and other improper conduct related to HHS grants
candidate_rules.source_title: Types of Civil Monetary Penalties and Affirmative Exclusions | Office of Inspector General | HHS
candidate_rules.statement: The OIG may impose civil monetary penalties (CMPs), assessments, and exclusions against individuals and entities that engage in fraud and other improper conduct related to HHS grants, contracts, and other agreements.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The administrative review process consists of several steps, which usually must be requested within certain time periods
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 20 CFR Part 404 Subpart J -- Determinations, Administrative Review Process, and Reopening of Determinations and Decisions
candidate_rules.statement: The Social Security Administration administrative review process consists of several ordered steps: (1) initial determination, (2) reconsideration, (3) hearing before an administrative law judge, (4) Appeals Council review, and (5) Federal court review.

candidate_rules.citation_text: A decision on an appeal must be made in writing by the component within 20 business days after receipt of the appeal.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 31 CFR 1.6 -- Administrative appeals.
candidate_rules.statement: Under 31 CFR 1.6, a decision on an administrative appeal must be made in writing by the component within 20 business days after receipt of the appeal, and a decision upholding a component's determination must contain a statement identifying the reasons for the affirmance, including any FOIA exemptions applied.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Every claimant has the right to written notice of the decision made on his or her claim, the right to a hearing, and the right of representation.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 38 CFR 3.103 -- Procedural due process and other rights.
candidate_rules.statement: Under 38 CFR 3.103, every VA claimant has the right to written notice of the decision made on his or her claim, the right to a hearing, and the right of representation; proceedings before VA are ex parte in nature and VA is obligated to assist a claimant in developing the facts pertinent to the claim.

candidate_rules.citation_text: ensure that DOT enforcement actions satisfy principles of due process and remain lawful, reasonable, and consistent with current Departmental and Administration policy
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register :: Administrative Rulemaking, Guidance, and Enforcement Procedures
candidate_rules.statement: DOT proposed enforcement procedures establish standard operating procedures within the Department's various enforcement programs intended to ensure that DOT enforcement actions satisfy principles of due process and remain lawful, reasonable, and consistent with current Departmental and Administration policy.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The FCA provides that any person who knowingly submits, or causes to submit, false claims to the government is liable for three times the government's damages plus a penalty that is linked to inflation.
candidate_rules.source_title: The False Claims Act | Civil Division | U.S. Department of Justice
candidate_rules.statement: Any person who knowingly submits, or causes to submit, false claims to the government is liable for three times the government's damages plus an inflation-linked penalty per claim under the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3733).

candidate_rules.citation_text: The civil FCA defines 'knowing' to include not only actual knowledge but also instances in which the person acted in deliberate ignorance or reckless disregard of the truth or falsity of the information.
candidate_rules.source_title: Fraud & Abuse Laws | Office of Inspector General | HHS
candidate_rules.statement: Under the civil False Claims Act, 'knowing' is defined to include not only actual knowledge but also deliberate ignorance or reckless disregard of the truth or falsity of the information; no specific intent to defraud is required.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The offense is classified as a felony and is punishable by a fine of up to $100,000 and imprisonment for up to 10 years.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: Solicitation of Proposals for New and Modified Safe Harbors and Special Fraud Alerts
candidate_rules.statement: The Anti-Kickback Statute (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b)) prohibits knowingly and willfully offering, paying, soliciting, or receiving remuneration to induce or reward referrals or purchases of items or services reimbursable under Federal health care programs; the offense is a felony punishable by fines up to $100,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Compliance with a safe harbor is not required, and arrangements that do not qualify for safe harbor protection are evaluated based on the totality of the facts and circumstances of the specific arrangement.
candidate_rules.source_title: General Questions Regarding Certain Fraud and Abuse Authorities | OIG | HHS
candidate_rules.statement: Safe harbor regulations under the Anti-Kickback Statute (42 CFR part 1001) specify payment and business practices that will not be subject to criminal prosecution or program exclusion; compliance with a safe harbor is voluntary, and arrangements not fitting a safe harbor are evaluated on the totality of facts and circumstances.

candidate_rules.citation_text: OIG is legally required to exclude from participation in all Federal health care programs individuals and entities convicted of the following types of criminal offenses: (1) Medicare or Medicaid fraud...
candidate_rules.source_title: Fraud & Abuse Laws | Office of Inspector General | HHS
candidate_rules.statement: OIG is legally required to exclude from participation in all Federal health care programs any individual or entity convicted of: (1) Medicare or Medicaid fraud; (2) patient abuse or neglect; (3) felony convictions for health-care-related fraud, theft, or financial misconduct; or (4) felony convictions for unlawful manufacture, distribution, prescription, or dispensing of controlled substances.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Mandatory exclusions must be imposed for a minimum 5-year period.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: Health Care Programs: Fraud and Abuse; Revisions to OIG's Exclusion Authorities (Dec. 2, 2024)
candidate_rules.statement: Mandatory OIG exclusions from Federal health care programs must be imposed for a minimum 5-year period; permissive exclusions may be derivative (based on prior court or agency actions) or non-derivative (based on OIG-initiated misconduct determinations), with no specified minimum period.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Penalties range from $10,000 to $50,000 per violation.
candidate_rules.source_title: Fraud & Abuse Laws | Office of Inspector General | HHS
candidate_rules.statement: Under the Civil Monetary Penalties Law (CMPL), OIG may seek penalties ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 per violation for conduct including presenting claims known to be false or fraudulent, and may also seek exclusion from Federal health care programs.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Section 3730(d)(1) of the FCA provides...that a qui tam relator...shall receive at least 15 percent but not more than 25 percent of the proceeds of the FCA action.
candidate_rules.source_title: The False Claims Act (FCA) — CMS/HHS Guidance Document
candidate_rules.statement: Under the civil FCA, a whistleblower (qui tam relator) who files suit on behalf of the United States is entitled to between 15% and 25% of proceeds when the government intervenes, and between 25% and 30% when the government does not intervene.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The State must develop and implement procedures for referring suspected fraud and abuse cases to the State program integrity unit...and to appropriate law enforcement officials.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 42 CFR 457.915 — Fraud detection and investigation
candidate_rules.statement: Under 42 CFR 457.915, states must develop and implement procedures for referring suspected fraud and abuse cases to the state program integrity unit and to appropriate law enforcement officials, including HHS-OIG and DOJ.

candidate_rules.citation_text: States must comply with all Federal laws and regulations designed to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse, including, but not limited to applicable provisions of Federal criminal law, the False Claims Act.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 42 CFR 495.368 — Combating fraud and abuse
candidate_rules.statement: Under 42 CFR 495.368, states must comply with all Federal laws and regulations designed to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse, including applicable provisions of Federal criminal law and the False Claims Act.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Under the Program, DOJ and HHS should make maximum use of all available remedies to fight health care fraud and abuse.
candidate_rules.source_title: Justice Manual | 978. Health Care Fraud and Abuse Control Program and Guidelines | DOJ
candidate_rules.statement: Under the Health Care Fraud and Abuse Control Program (HIPAA), DOJ and HHS must make maximum use of all available remedies — criminal, civil, and administrative — to fight health care fraud and abuse, including joint and parallel investigations and proceedings.

candidate_rules.citation_text: enforcement efforts rely principally on five rather general statutes: 18 U.S.C. §§ 287 (false claims), 371 (conspiracy), 1001 (false statements), 1341 (mail fraud) and 1343 (wire fraud).
candidate_rules.source_title: Justice Manual | 901. Scope of the General Statutes Prohibiting Fraud Against the Government | DOJ
candidate_rules.statement: Federal enforcement of fraud against the government relies principally on five general statutes: 18 U.S.C. §§ 287 (false claims), 371 (conspiracy), 1001 (false statements), 1341 (mail fraud), and 1343 (wire fraud).

candidate_rules.citation_text: Employees shall...report fraud, waste, abuse, and corruption in Commission programs, including on the part of Commission employees, contractors, subcontractors, grantees, or other recipients of Commission financial assistance, to the Office of Inspector General.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 18 CFR 3c.3 — Reporting fraud, waste, abuse, and corruption and cooperation with official inquiries
candidate_rules.statement: Under 18 CFR 3c.3, federal employees are required to report fraud, waste, abuse, and corruption in Commission programs — including by contractors, subcontractors, grantees, or other recipients of Commission financial assistance — to the Office of Inspector General or other appropriate Federal authority.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Prohibits a physician from referring Medicare patients for designated health services to an entity with which the physician (or immediate family member) has a financial relationship, unless an exception applies.
candidate_rules.source_title: HEAT Provider Compliance Training: Stark Law and AKS Comparison Chart | OIG HHS
candidate_rules.statement: The Physician Self-Referral Law (Stark Law, 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn) prohibits a physician from referring Medicare patients for designated health services to an entity with which the physician or an immediate family member has a financial relationship, unless a specific exception applies; the designated health services entity is also prohibited from submitting claims to Medicare for services resulting from a prohibited referral.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Federal agencies may administratively pursue these 'small' false claims and certified false statements within six years of the claim being made.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: Implementation of the Administrative False Claims Act (Nov. 3, 2025)
candidate_rules.statement: Under the Program Fraud Civil Remedies Act (PFCRA, 31 U.S.C. 3801–12), federal agencies may administratively pursue false claims of $1,000,000 or less when DOJ elects not to pursue FCA remedies; a person may be penalized $5,000 per claim or statement and assessed up to double the amount falsely claimed, within six years of the claim being made.

candidate_rules.citation_text: OIG periodically issues Special Fraud Alerts to give continuing guidance to health care industry stakeholders about practices that OIG considers to be suspect or of particular concern.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register: Solicitation of Proposals for New and Modified Safe Harbors and Special Fraud Alerts (Nov. 27, 2024)
candidate_rules.statement: OIG issues Special Fraud Alerts to give continuing guidance to health care industry stakeholders about practices considered suspect or of particular concern; these alerts encourage industry compliance and are published periodically.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Old-age and survivors insurance benefit payments · Sec. 203. Reduction of insurance benefits · Sec. 204. Overpayments and underpayments
candidate_rules.source_title: Social Security Act Title II – SSA.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Title II of the Social Security Act establishes the Federal Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OASDI) program, providing benefits to insured workers who have attained old age, become disabled, or died, and to their eligible dependents and survivors.

candidate_rules.citation_text: the amount of a monthly insurance benefit of any individual for each month under subsection (b), (c), (e), (f), or (g) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by an amount equal to two-thirds of the amount of any monthly periodic benefit payable
candidate_rules.source_title: Social Security Act §202 – SSA.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Under Social Security Act §202, monthly insurance benefit amounts for dependents (wife, divorced wife, husband, divorced husband, child) may be reduced by two-thirds of any monthly periodic benefit payable based on earnings in non-covered federal or state government service during the last 60 months of such service.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Subpart B relates to quarters of coverage and insured status requirements … Subpart D relates to the requirements for entitlement to monthly benefits
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 20 CFR Part 404 – Federal Old-Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance (1950-)
candidate_rules.statement: 20 CFR Part 404, Subpart B governs quarters of coverage and insured status requirements for Social Security OASDI benefits; Subpart D sets out requirements for entitlement to monthly benefits, how benefit amounts are figured, when rights to benefits begin and end, and how family relationships are determined.

candidate_rules.citation_text: If you are entitled to cash benefits or to a period of disability because you are disabled, you should promptly tell us if—
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 20 CFR Part 404 Subpart P – Continuing or Stopping Disability
candidate_rules.statement: Under 20 CFR Part 404, if a beneficiary is entitled to cash benefits or a period of disability because of disability, they must promptly report changes to SSA; SSA may reduce reporting responsibilities if it has authorization to obtain wage and employment information from a payroll data provider.

candidate_rules.citation_text: This Title XVI appears in the United States Code as §§1381-1383f, subchapter XVI, chapter 7, Title 42.
candidate_rules.source_title: Social Security Act Title XVI – SSA.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Title XVI of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. §§1381–1383f) establishes the Supplemental Security Income (SSI) program, a means-tested, federally administered income assistance program providing monthly cash payments to needy aged (65+), blind, and disabled individuals, including children under 18 with limited income and resources.

candidate_rules.citation_text: SSI eligibility is restricted to qualified persons who have countable resources/assets of not more than $2,000, or $3,000 for a couple.
candidate_rules.source_title: Supplemental Security Income (SSI) Program – Overview | ASPE (HHS)
candidate_rules.statement: Under Title XVI of the Social Security Act, SSI pays what is necessary to bring an individual's income up to the statutorily prescribed income floor; SSI eligibility is restricted to individuals with countable resources not exceeding $2,000 (or $3,000 for a couple).

candidate_rules.citation_text: You are eligible for supplemental security income (SSI) benefits if you are an aged, blind, or disabled person who meets the requirements described in subpart B and who has limited income and resources.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 20 CFR 416.1100 – Income and SSI Eligibility
candidate_rules.statement: Under 20 CFR §416.1100, a person is eligible for SSI benefits if they are an aged, blind, or disabled individual who meets the requirements in Subpart B of 20 CFR Part 416 and has limited income and resources; income is counted on a monthly basis and not all income is counted in determining eligibility and benefit amount.

candidate_rules.citation_text: When you file an application in the month that you meet all the other requirements for eligibility, the earliest month for which we can pay you benefits is the month following the month you filed the application.
candidate_rules.source_title: eCFR :: 20 CFR Part 416 Subpart C – Filing of Applications
candidate_rules.statement: Under 20 CFR Part 416 Subpart C, an SSI application is considered filed on the day it is received at a Social Security office or authorized location; when an application is filed in the month all other eligibility requirements are met, the earliest payable month is the month following the filing month.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Authorized by title IV-A of the Social Security Act, TANF is a block grant that provides states, territories, and tribes federal funds to design and operate a program to accomplish the purposes of TANF.
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register :: Strengthening TANF as a Safety Net and Work Program (HHS/ACF, Oct. 2023)
candidate_rules.statement: TANF is authorized by Title IV-A of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.), as established by the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (P.L. 104-193); it is a block grant providing federal funds to states, territories, and tribes to design programs assisting needy families so children may be cared for in their own homes, ending dependence on government benefits by promoting work, preventing out-of-wedlock pregnancies, and encouraging two-parent families.

candidate_rules.citation_text: states must adhere to the work participation rate and other federal requirements, such as a 60-month lifetime limit on an adult receiving federally funded assistance
candidate_rules.source_title: Federal Register :: Strengthening TANF as a Safety Net and Work Program (HHS/ACF, Oct. 2023)
candidate_rules.statement: Under Title IV-A of the Social Security Act, there is a 60-month (5-year) lifetime limit on an adult receiving federally funded TANF assistance; states must adhere to work participation rates and other federal requirements while retaining flexibility in designing their programs.

candidate_rules.citation_text: The state statutory citation for the legal authority under which the single state agency administers the state plan is: Welfare and Institutions Code Sections (W&I) 10720 et seq., 10740, 14100.1
candidate_rules.source_title: California Medicaid State Plan Amendment SPA 13-0024-MM4 – CMS/Medicaid.gov
candidate_rules.statement: The California single state agency administers the Medi-Cal (Medicaid) state plan under the legal authority of Welfare and Institutions Code Sections 10720 et seq., 10740, and 14100.1, and has authority to make rules and regulations binding on political subdivisions under W&I Code 10725 et seq., 10740, 10743, 10745, and 10800 et seq.

candidate_rules.citation_text: under the federal SUPPORT Act and State law (Welfare & Institutions Code § 14011.10 (e)(1) & (2)), the State and counties are prohibited from terminating Medicaid eligibility because the individual is...
candidate_rules.source_title: CalAIM Reentry Initiative Implementation Plan Approval – CMS/Medicaid.gov (October 2024)
candidate_rules.statement: Under California Welfare and Institutions Code § 14011.10(e)(1) & (2), the State and counties are prohibited from terminating Medicaid eligibility for individuals under age 21 or Former Foster Youth under age 26 solely because the individual is incarcerated.

candidate_rules.citation_text: reimbursement...will be at the lesser of usual charges or the limits specified in the California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 3, Chapter 3, Article 7 (commencing with Section 51501)
candidate_rules.source_title: California State Plan Amendment SPA CA-22-0013 – CMS/Medicaid.gov
candidate_rules.statement: Medi-Cal reimbursement for covered services is set at the lesser of usual charges or the limits specified in California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 3, Chapter 3, Article 7 (commencing with Section 51501), and CCR Title 17, Chapter 4, Subchapter 13, Sections 6800–6874 for EPSDT health assessment services, or as specified by any other means authorized by state law.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Medi-Cal Appeal — A request for a fair hearing in accordance with California Code of Regulations Title 22, section 51014.1 and Welfare and Institutions Code section 10950
candidate_rules.source_title: California Medicare-Medicaid Financial Alignment Initiative Contract – CMS.gov
candidate_rules.statement: A Medi-Cal appeal is defined as a request for a fair hearing in accordance with California Code of Regulations Title 22, Section 51014.1, and Welfare and Institutions Code Section 10950; all fair hearings conducted by CDSS are de novo fair hearings.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Each state administers a separate unemployment insurance program, but all states follow the same guidelines established by federal law.
candidate_rules.source_title: How Do I File for Unemployment Insurance? – U.S. Department of Labor
candidate_rules.statement: California's Unemployment Insurance program is authorized under state unemployment compensation laws in accordance with applicable federal law; each state administers a separate unemployment insurance program but all states follow the same guidelines established by federal law, and California's Employment Development Department (EDD) is the administering agency.

candidate_rules.citation_text: Unemployment Insurance Programs (Programs authorized under State unemployment compensation laws in accordance with applicable Federal law)
candidate_rules.source_title: WIOA State Plan for the State of California – U.S. Department of Education
candidate_rules.statement: California's Unemployment Insurance program is identified in the California WIOA State Plan as a program authorized under state unemployment compensation laws in accordance with applicable federal law, administered by the Employment Development Department (EDD).

candidate_rules.citation_text: A State may pay UC only to an individual who is able to work and available for work for the week for which UC is claimed.
candidate_rules.source_title: 20 CFR Part 604 – Regulations for Eligibility for Unemployment Compensation – eCFR
candidate_rules.statement: Under 20 CFR Part 604, a state may pay unemployment compensation (UC) only to an individual who is able to work and available for work for the week for which UC is claimed; whether an individual is able to work and available for work must be tested by determining whether the individual is offering services for which a labor market exists.

candidate_rules.citation_text: the Labor Department cited the state's poor performance in key areas, including an increasing improper payment rate, insufficient timeliness of payments, and the accuracy and quality of the state's data
candidate_rules.source_title: US Department of Labor to probe California's Unemployment Insurance program – DOL.gov (February 2026)
candidate_rules.statement: California's Employment Development Department is subject to federal oversight and reporting requirements for the UC program; the U.S. Department of Labor cited California EDD for an increasing improper payment rate, insufficient timeliness of payments, and data accuracy and quality deficiencies as part of federal compliance monitoring.

candidate_rules.citation_text: FNS approved the California Department of Social Services (DSS) extension request to waive the statutory definition of 'food' under Section 3(k)(1) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, as amended and accompanying regulations at 7 CFR 271.2
candidate_rules.source_title: California Disaster Nutrition Assistance – USDA Food and Nutrition Service
candidate_rules.statement: California's SNAP program (known as CalFresh) is administered by the California Department of Social Services (DSS) under the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008; FNS approved California DSS requests to waive the statutory definition of 'food' under Section 3(k)(1) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 and accompanying regulations at 7 CFR 271.2 for disaster-affected counties.

candidate_rules.citation_text: SNAP is designed to promote the general welfare and to safeguard the health and well-being of the Nation's population by raising the levels of nutrition among low-income households.
candidate_rules.source_title: 7 CFR Part 271 – General Information and Definitions – eCFR
candidate_rules.statement: Under the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 CFR 271.2), SNAP is designed to promote the general welfare and safeguard the health and well-being of the nation's population by raising nutrition levels among low-income households; California administers this program as CalFresh through the California Department of Social Services.
